newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian official curbs unfermented cocoa trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian official curbs unfermented cocoa trade.

text.p: The governor of Indonesia's key cocoa growing region of South Sulawesi has ordered farmers to stop selling unfermented cocoa beans, according to a document obtained by Reuters on Tuesday.

The official document issued by the governor said that all parties involved in buying cocoa should stop purchasing unfermented cocoa beans effective November 16, the date when the instructions were issued.

The document, signed by governor Zainal Basri Palaguna, calls on all government departments and agencies down to the village level, to take steps to ensure that there is no trade in unfermented cocoa beans.
The document, however, does not stipulate penalties for those breaching the order.
Palaguna said in the document the move was aimed at helping improve the quality of cocoa being traded in South Sulawesi.
Cocoa traders in South Sulawesi capital Ujung Pandang said on Tuesday that only about 10 percent of the cocoa beans traded in the region are fermented.
They said South Sulawesi accounts for nearly 60 percent of Indonesia's total cocoa production, estimated by trade sources to total 260,000-270,000 tonnes this year.
The Indonesia Cocoa Association has forecast 1996 output at 290,000 tonnes.
"I think this will have an impact on cocoa exports from South Sulawesi because I expect more stringent checks of beans we are exporting," one trader said.
"This could also result in more beans being sold domestically," he added.
Another trader said success would depend on how effectively the governor's instructions are carried out.
"Having to ferment the beans for about five days means there will be a slowdown in the availability of beans," he added.
The document also states that the governor has instructed that all coffee sold in South Sulawesi should be processed, but did not give details.
